concepts.title: Totipotency and the History of Plant Tissue Culture
concepts.definition: Every living plant cell keeps the totipotent power to regenerate a whole plant, the intuition Haberlandt advanced in 1902 that earned him the fatherhood of the field; kinetin arrived in 1955, the Skoog-Miller 1957 ratio rule tied organ fate to hormone balance, Murashige and Skoog's 1962 salt-rich medium became the standard, and Guha and Maheshwari's 1964 anther-culture haploids opened the door to somatic hybrids, Pomato of 1978 and the somaclonal variation named in 1981.
concepts.key_idea: One vegetative cell can rebuild the entire plant - the promise that turned tissue culture into both a science and an industry.
question_patterns: who is regarded as the father of plant tissue culture and which 1902 idea earned that title
define totipotency and explain why it underlies all plant tissue culture
which 1957 hypothesis tied root and shoot differentiation to the auxin kinetin ratio
why did the 1962 Murashige and Skoog medium become the most widely used formulation
who produced the first androgenic haploid Datura plants and through which culture
arrange the landmarks from kinetin discovery to the naming of somaclonal variation in date order

solution_steps.explain: Totipotency lets a differentiated vegetative cell divide and redifferentiate into any specialised cell or whole plant.
1902 concept, 1955 kinetin, 1957 ratio rule, 1962 MS medium, 1964 haploid Datura, 1972 somatic hybrid.
Each landmark enabled a modern use - regeneration, haploid breeding, somatic hybridisation and variation screening.

worked_examples.q: Who advanced the totipotency intuition in 1902: Haberlandt or Skoog?

concepts.title: Explant Preparation and Culture Steps
concepts.definition: Culturing starts with an explant - meristem, leaf, cotyledon, hypocotyl or embryo - surface-sterilised in sodium hypochlorite, rinsed and inoculated onto sterile medium; the tissue then dedifferentiates into callus, redifferentiates organ primordia through organogenesis or follows somatic embryogenesis, with regenerated shoots rooted and plantlets hardened toward the field, immature embryos responding best among explant choices.
concepts.key_idea: Sterilise, inoculate, dedifferentiate, redifferentiate, root and harden - the pipeline from explant to field-ready plantlet.
question_patterns: list the sequential steps of plant tissue culture from explant selection to field transfer
define explant and name five tissues commonly used as explants
which disinfectant is most commonly used for surface sterilisation of explants

solution_steps.explain: Select the explant and disinfect with sodium hypochlorite, then rinse in sterile water.
Inoculate onto medium; cells dedifferentiate into callus and then redifferentiate shoots, roots or somatic embryos.
Excise shoots to rooting medium, then harden plantlets in soil before field transfer.

worked_examples.q: The starting tissue piece in culture is called an what: explant or implant?

concepts.title: Auxin Cytokinin Balance in Nutrient Media
concepts.definition: Media blend macronutrients, micronutrients, amino acids, B vitamins, two to five percent sucrose, gelling agar, optional antibiotics and minute doses of five hormone classes; the auxin-cytokinin ratio rules morphogenesis - excess auxin roots, excess cytokinin shoots, and intermediate balance proliferates callus - while a pH set around 5.8-6.0 keeps the gel firm and the salts soluble.
concepts.key_idea: Divide auxin by cytokinin - a quotient above one pushes roots, below one pushes shoots, near one keeps callus.
question_patterns: a medium carries 2 mg per litre auxin and 0.5 mg per litre kinetin - compute the ratio and predict the organ that regenerates

what happens to medium hardness when pH rises or falls

solution_steps.explain: The auxin-to-cytokinin quotient predicts the morphogenic fate.
A positive difference marks auxin dominance and rooting; negative marks shoot dominance.

concepts.title: MS Medium Strength versus White Medium
concepts.definition: Murashige and Skoog's formulation is a salt powerhouse next to White's classic recipe: potassium nitrate runs 1900 against 80 milligrams per litre and ammonium nitrate adds 1650 where White has none, thiamine sits at 0.5 rather than 0.01, and sucrose rises from 20 to 30 grams per litre - richness that lets MS culture a far wider range of species.
concepts.key_idea: Divide each MS concentration by its White's value to see how much stronger the modern medium is.

solution_steps.explain: The quotient shows the fold enrichment of MS over White's.
The difference gives the extra milligrams per litre supplied.

concepts.title: Micropropagation and Synthetic Seeds
concepts.definition: Micropropagation clones elite, rare or non-fertile plants season-free in flasks - India alone regenerates over 400 million banana plantlets a year - while synthetic seeds encapsulate somatic embryos in calcium alginate coats loaded with nutrients and regulators, storing and shipping clonal stock of carrot, grape or sandalwood without any seed at all.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply one elite genotype into millions, then pack the embryos in alginate beads that behave like true seeds.
question_patterns: what is micropropagation and how does it beat traditional vegetative propagation

solution_steps.explain: Sterile explants regenerate shoots repeatedly under controlled light and temperature.
Somatic embryos drop into calcium alginate with nutrients and growth regulators.
Synthetic seeds keep and germinate like normal seed for mass clonal propagation.

worked_examples.q: Synthetic seeds encapsulate somatic embryos in coats of what: calcium alginate or plastic?

concepts.title: Haploids Double Haploids and Somatic Hybrids
concepts.definition: Anther, pollen or ovary culture yields haploids whose colchicine doubling produces homozygous diploids that expose recessive traits for breeders; protoplasts stripped by cellulase and pectinase fuse under polyethylene glycol across species barriers - Carlson's 1972 Nicotiana hybrids began the era, Pomato mixed potato with tomato, and cybridisation even pairs one parent's nucleus with another's mitochondria or chloroplasts.
concepts.key_idea: Double the haploid chromosome set with colchicine and the clone turns homozygous diploid; fuse protoplasts and species barriers fall.
question_patterns: a haploid rice plant carries 12 chromosomes - how many chromosomes does its colchicine-doubled derivative carry

solution_steps.explain: Colchicine converts each haploid chromosome count to diploid.
The doubled plant is a homozygous diploid ready for crossing.

concepts.title: Meristem Culture for Virus-Free Plants
concepts.definition: Viruses scatter unevenly through plant bodies and leave the apical and axillary meristems clean, so excising a meristem tip shorter than one millimetre and culturing it regenerates sugarcane, banana or potato stock entirely free of virus - rescuing yields in clonally propagated crops where every infected cutting infects its whole lineage.
concepts.key_idea: Take the tiniest meristem - under a millimetre - where no virus has reached, and grow a clean clone from it.
question_patterns: why are apical and axillary meristems free of virus particles

solution_steps.explain: Dissect a sub-millimetre apical or axillary meristem under sterile conditions.
Culture the tip onto medium to rebuild a whole plantlet.
Test the plantlets for virus, then bulk up the clean stock by micropropagation.

worked_examples.q: Meristem tips shorter than what length yield virus-free plants: one millimetre or one centimetre?

concepts.title: Somaclonal Variation and Secondary Metabolites
concepts.definition: Culture both creates and harvests plant chemistry: somaclonal variations - the term Larkin and Scowcroft coined in 1981 - pass somatic mutations into regenerated plants, a bane for clonal fidelity but a boon yielding disease-resistant sugarcane, banana and tomato cultivars; meanwhile cell suspensions and hairy roots overproduce secondary metabolites from artemisinin and azadirachtin to taxol, shikonin and vincristine, independent of season and without stripping wild populations.
concepts.key_idea: Culture-induced variants can be screened as new cultivars, and cultured cells can out-produce the whole plant in valuable metabolites.
question_patterns: define somaclonal variation and name the scientists who introduced the term
why can somaclonal variation be both a boon and a bane in tissue culture

solution_steps.explain: Long-term callus or suspension culture accumulates and expresses somatic mutations in regenerants.
Select regenerants with agronomically useful novel phenotypes.
Parallel cell or hairy-root cultures scale up secondary metabolite yields under controlled conditions.

worked_examples.q: Who coined the term somaclonal variation in 1981: Larkin and Scowcroft, or Haberlandt?
